title: AXI Per-ID Read and Reorder-Safe Scoreboard
description: Execute AR allocation, exact R beat/RLAST retirement, different-ID response reordering, same-ID FIFO checks, ID restoration, data comparison, and configured depth guards.
learnerQuestion: How does a scoreboard accept legal completion reordering without losing per-ID order or end-to-end data attribution?
protocolScope: AXI3 / AXI4 read and response order

configurations.label: Read depth 4
configurations.description: Four total reads, two per ID, independently counted from write outstanding state.

configurations.label: Fabric ID remap
configurations.description: Source-port context is retained internally and original RID restored at the master interface.

scenarios.label: Read gaps and R backpressure
scenarios.description: AR acceptance allocates one queue entry; the subordinate may insert R gaps, but once RVALID is asserted the complete payload remains stable until each beat is accepted.

checks.label: AR allocates per-ID state
checks.evidence: The request remains outstanding through the accepted final R beat.

checks.label: Gap does not consume a beat
checks.evidence: A product liveness contract can bound the gap, but base AXI does not invent a transfer.

checks.label: Complete R payload retained
checks.evidence: The subordinate source retains all R payload signals until acceptance.

steps.label: Accept final R
steps.event: Beat 1 and beat 2 accepted; RLAST=1 on beat 2

checks.label: RLAST on exact accepted beat
checks.evidence: Gap and stalled cycles never advance the beat count.

checks.label: Accepted RLAST retires request
checks.evidence: The per-ID head retires only on RVALID && RREADY && RLAST.

scenarios.label: Early RLAST failure
scenarios.description: RLAST on accepted beat 2 of a four-beat request is the first failing accepted edge; recovery after the violation is implementation-defined.

steps.label: Accept early RLAST
steps.event: RID3 beat 2 handshakes with RLAST=1, expected beat 4

checks.label: RLAST must match accepted beat count
checks.evidence: The checker reports this accepted edge and keeps the declared request length as the expectation.

scenarios.label: Legal different-ID completion
scenarios.description: Read B can complete before A because their IDs differ; data comparison selects the correct expected per-ID head.

checks.label: Read depth within limit
checks.evidence: Read and write counters remain separate.

checks.label: Per-ID FIFO allocated
checks.evidence: Same numeric ID can be reused by queueing additional ordered entries.

checks.label: Data uses RID-selected expectation
checks.evidence: End-to-end comparison is independent of global completion order.

checks.label: Accepted RLAST retires B
checks.evidence: Only B retired; A remains in the ID0 queue.

steps.label: Retire A
steps.event: Two RID0 beats, RLAST on accepted beat 2

checks.label: Exact accepted beat count
checks.evidence: R stalls do not advance the per-transaction counter.

checks.label: All reads retired
checks.evidence: Each accepted AR has one accepted final R retirement.

scenarios.label: Corrupt same-ID reorder
scenarios.description: Two ID0 requests A then C cannot return C first because RID alone cannot distinguish them.

steps.label: Return C before A
steps.event: RID0 data=C0 while per-ID head is A

checks.label: Per-ID head must respond first
checks.evidence: The scoreboard flags the first accepted corrupt RID0 beat.

scenarios.label: Source-scoped ID restoration
scenarios.description: Two masters reuse local ID5; internal route IDs differ and responses restore each original local RID.

checks.label: Internal ownership stays distinct
checks.evidence: The fabric can append, remap, or retain metadata; it must preserve source attribution.

steps.label: Restore responses
steps.event: 0x25 returns to M1 as RID5; 0x15 returns to M0 as RID5

checks.label: No response misroute
checks.evidence: Different completion order does not change source ownership or local ID restoration.

traceability.requirement: AXI-R per-ID order and exact LAST
traceability.stimulus: same/different IDs, R gaps and R backpressure
traceability.coverage: ID relation × completion order × RLAST position × depth
source × local ID × target × completion order
